tasks.short: Handle questions from managers and staff, explain CAO and contract terms, and help sort out conflicts on the floor.

today.trigger: A manager, employee or OR member calls, sends a Teams message or emails with a question or a problem (a schedule dispute, a contract question, a conflict on shift).
steps: Read the question and find the employee's contract, function scale and history in AFAS Profit
Look up the relevant article in the CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer or the warehouse CAO and any local agreement on SharePoint
Talk to the manager and the employee, often separately, sometimes on site in Tilburg or Venlo
Agree an outcome and record it in AFAS or a file note, then follow up by email
drudgery: Searching CAO PDFs and old emails for the right article and past decisions
Rewriting the same explanation for different managers
Writing file notes after each conversation
today.time_sinks: Collecting the facts and precedent before a conversation, and writing up afterwards; the conversation itself is the valuable part.

lenses.faster: A case briefing pulls the employee's contract, scale, absence and earlier file notes from AFAS plus the matching CAO articles, so preparation drops from half an hour to a few minutes.
lenses.autonomous: When a case is logged, the briefing and a draft file note template are created without the HRBP asking; follow-up reminders are set from the agreed actions.
lenses.ambitious: Every manager issue gets a recorded outcome and a searchable precedent, so the three sites handle similar cases the same way for the first time.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses digging through CAO PDFs and writing notes from memory; what stays is the actual conversation and solving the problem.
lenses.options: For a dispute, the copilot drafts two or three possible resolutions with the CAO basis and the risk of each, so the HRBP walks in with choices.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP maintains the case taxonomy and precedent library and reviews where cases cluster (a site, a manager, a shift pattern) instead of reacting case by case.
reach: First-line contract questions now handled by the HR Administrator
Spotting patterns that the People Analytics Analyst would otherwise report on

tasks.human_edge: Trust with both sides, reading tension in a room, and judgement on fairness and works-council sensitivity cannot be delegated.
tasks.pattern_why: The work is relational and judgement-heavy; AI helps with the briefing, precedent and write-up while the HRBP leads the conversation.

in_practice.trigger: A case is opened from an email or Teams message in a shared HR case list.
steps: Copilot builds a briefing from AFAS employee data, CAO articles on SharePoint and earlier case notes
HRBP reviews the briefing and suggested options before talking to the parties
After the meeting the HRBP dictates key points; the copilot drafts the file note and follow-up email
HRBP edits and files the note in AFAS and sends the email
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP approves every file note and message; no outcome is communicated without them.
data_needed: Employee contract and function data from AFAS
Current CAO texts and local agreements
Earlier anonymised case outcomes
in_practice.logs_to: Case note on the employee file in AFAS Profit and a case list on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can summarise documents and draft emails grounded on SharePoint and Outlook content.
Preparation and write-up make up a large part of case handling time for HR business partners.

risks: Sensitive personal data (health, conflict) processed by an AI tool without a DPIA under AVG
Briefing misreads which CAO applies to a person (transport vs warehouse)
Employees feel the HRBP relies on a tool instead of listening
research_questions: How much of a typical case's time is preparation and write-up versus conversation? Track 20 cases.
Can Copilot be restricted to the right AFAS and SharePoint sources with access controls the OR accepts?
Are past case notes consistent enough to use as precedent?

tasks.short: Explain HR policies, CAO rules, leave, verzuim and labour law to managers and employees.

today.trigger: A recurring question arrives: leave entitlement, overtime pay under the CAO, shift allowances, sick reporting rules, notice periods, flex worker rules.
steps: Identify which CAO and policy applies to the person
Look up the article in the CAO, the personnel handbook on SharePoint or wet- en regelgeving
Check the person's data in AFAS if the answer depends on it
Write or tell the answer, often in Dutch and sometimes in Polish or English for flex workers
drudgery: Answering the same leave and allowance questions many times a week
Keeping track of which version of a policy is current
today.time_sinks: High volume of repeat questions that each need a lookup and a careful written answer.

lenses.faster: A policy assistant in Teams answers routine questions with the CAO article quoted, so the HRBP only sees the harder ones.
lenses.autonomous: Employees and managers ask the assistant directly at any time, including night shifts; answers that touch a personal right or a dispute are routed to HR.
lenses.ambitious: Shift workers in Venlo and Rotterdam get a correct answer in their own language within minutes, which they rarely get today.
lenses.joy: The HRBP stops typing the 40th explanation of holiday hours; what remains is the unclear cases where interpretation matters.
lenses.options: For an ambiguous rule, the assistant shows the readings and their basis so HR can pick and then publish one standard interpretation.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP owns the knowledge base: approves sources, reviews wrong or escalated answers weekly and fixes the policy text that causes confusion.
reach: Tier-one questions now handled by HR Administrators
Payroll Specialist questions on allowances and overtime
Explaining onboarding rules that Recruiters get asked about

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting grey areas, knowing local agreements and the history with the OR, and giving answers that carry legal weight.
tasks.pattern_why: Answering from a fixed set of sources is reliable for routine questions, but answers affecting rights or disputes need a person to check before they count.

in_practice.trigger: A question is posted in a Teams HR assistant or sent to the HR mailbox.
steps: Assistant classifies the question and finds the applicable CAO or policy by employee group
It answers with the source article quoted and a link to the document
Questions about a personal entitlement, dismissal, sickness or a complaint are routed to the HRBP with a draft answer
HRBP reviews a weekly sample and all routed answers, and updates sources when answers are wrong
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP approves every routed answer; routine answers are sampled weekly.
data_needed: Current CAO texts and personnel handbook
Mapping of employees to CAO and site
Approved interpretations of unclear articles
in_practice.logs_to: Question and answer log on SharePoint with the source cited and a flag for escalation

evidence.claim: Copilot Studio can build Teams agents that answer from SharePoint documents.
HR service platforms offer virtual agents for employee policy questions.

risks: A wrong answer on pay or dismissal creates a legal claim or OR conflict
Outdated CAO version in the sources
Works council right of consent (WOR art. 27) may apply to introducing such a system
research_questions: What share of incoming questions is routine and fully answered by a CAO or policy text? Classify one month of the HR mailbox.
How accurate are answers on a test set of 100 real questions, checked by an HRBP?
Will the OR consent and what logging do they require?
Do shift workers actually use Teams on their phones?

tasks.short: Help managers place people in the right roles and teams, including moves between sites and shifts.

today.trigger: A vacancy, reorganisation, a return-to-work after long absence, or seasonal peak asks for people to be moved or matched.
steps: Collect who is available from AFAS (function, contract hours, site) and Studytube (forklift, VCA certificates)
Talk to managers about needs and to employees about wishes and limits
Build an Excel overview of candidates for each position
Agree placements and arrange contract changes with the HR Administrator
drudgery: Merging AFAS and Studytube exports by hand in Excel
today.time_sinks: Building a reliable picture of who is available and qualified before any real discussion.

lenses.faster: A standing Power BI view joins AFAS function and contract data with Studytube certificates, so the candidate list is ready in minutes.
lenses.autonomous: Expiring certificates and open positions are flagged each night, so the HRBP sees matching gaps before the manager asks.
lenses.ambitious: Internal moves get checked first for every vacancy, so fewer roles go to agencies or external hires and more people grow inside.
lenses.joy: No more Excel merges; time goes to talking with people about what they want.
lenses.options: For a peak or reorganisation, two or three placement scenarios with the cost, flex need and certificate gaps of each.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP defines the matching rules (skills, certificates, CAO constraints, restrictions from the bedrijfsarts) and checks the output rather than compiling lists.
reach: Internal mobility work of the Recruiters
Training needs input for the L&D Specialists
Flex demand input for the agency orders

tasks.human_edge: Knowing people's ambitions, team dynamics and personal limits, and handling the conversation when someone does not get a role.
tasks.pattern_why: Availability and qualification matching is rule-based on structured AFAS and Studytube data; the choice stays with people.

in_practice.trigger: A position opens or a placement request is logged; the data view is refreshed nightly.
steps: Nightly job joins AFAS employee data and Studytube certificates in Power BI
For a position, the view filters by site, function, contract hours and required certificates
HRBP adds context from conversations and narrows to a shortlist
Manager and HRBP decide; the HR Administrator processes the change in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Manager and HRBP decide every placement; the tool only lists candidates.
data_needed: Function, site, contract hours from AFAS
Certificates and expiry dates from Studytube
Work restrictions (without medical detail) from the absence file
in_practice.logs_to: Placement decisions in AFAS Profit; matching view snapshots in Power BI

evidence.claim: Power BI can combine data from several exports into a refreshed report.
Matching people to roles on certificates and contract data is rule-based and does not need a model.

risks: Using health-related restrictions in matching breaches AVG rules on medical data
Automated ranking of employees for roles may count as high-risk AI under the EU AI Act if a model is used
Data quality in Studytube certificates is incomplete
research_questions: How complete and current are certificate records in Studytube?
How often per month does a placement need this overview, and how long does it take today?
Can the Studytube data be extracted into the nightly Power BI refresh?

tasks.short: Advise managers on how to recruit and keep people, such as warehouse staff who leave within 90 days.

today.trigger: A site has high turnover, slow hiring, or a manager asks for help with a recruiting or retention plan.
steps: Pull turnover, time-to-hire and 90-day retention figures from Power BI and Recruitee
Interview managers and read exit interview notes
Draft a proposal (referral bonus, onboarding buddy, shift choice, pay check against market)
Present to the manager or HR Director and agree actions
drudgery: Combining Recruitee and AFAS figures by hand
Reading exit notes one by one
today.time_sinks: Gathering and cleaning the numbers and the reasons people leave before the advice can be formed.

lenses.faster: Retention data per site, shift and hiring source is ready in a dashboard and exit notes are summarised into themes, so the HRBP starts at the analysis.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly signal flags teams where 90-day leavers rise, with the main reasons from exit and stay interviews.
lenses.ambitious: Each site gets a retention plan reviewed every quarter, tied to the North Star, instead of advice only when a manager asks.
lenses.joy: Less Excel and fewer slides; more time testing ideas with team leaders.
lenses.options: The copilot drafts three to five interventions with expected cost and effect, so the manager chooses rather than gets one proposal.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP runs small experiments (for example buddy system in Tilburg only) and measures them, improving the playbook.
reach: Analysis work of the People Analytics Analyst
Employer branding input for the Recruiters
Cost cases with the FP&A Analysts

tasks.human_edge: Credibility with managers, knowing what is realistic on a site, and judgement on pay and CAO constraints.
tasks.pattern_why: The HRBP leads the advice; AI speeds up the data, themes and option drafts.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly retention signal or a manager request.
steps: Power BI shows 90-day retention and time to hire by site, team and source
LLM groups exit interview notes into themes with counts
Copilot drafts options with cost estimates
HRBP picks and adapts, then discusses with the manager
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP decides what to advise; any pay or policy change goes through the HR Director and, where needed, the OR.
data_needed: Hire and leave dates by site and source
Exit interview notes
Agency flex worker conversion data
in_practice.logs_to: Advice and agreed actions on a SharePoint retention page per site

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can describe trends and answer questions on a report.
LLMs can group free-text exit comments into themes reliably enough for a person to check.

risks: Small teams make exit themes traceable to individuals (AVG)
Advice built on dashboards that miss flex worker data
Managers take generated options as tested
research_questions: Are exit interviews recorded consistently enough to analyse?
Can Recruitee hire data be linked to AFAS records to measure 90-day retention per source?
Which past retention actions had measurable effect?

tasks.short: Coach and train managers on interviewing, performance talks, difficult conversations and documenting performance issues.

today.trigger: A new team leader starts, the annual performance cycle begins, or a manager must deal with an underperforming employee.
steps: Prepare or update training slides and handouts
Give a session or one-to-one coaching
Review the manager's draft documentation (warnings, improvement plans)
Correct the file so it holds up legally if it goes to the UWV or court
drudgery: Repeating the same basics to each new team leader
today.time_sinks: Fixing weak documentation after the fact and repeating basic training one-to-one.

lenses.faster: A template assistant helps managers write a factual, dated performance note, so the HRBP reviews instead of rewrites.
lenses.autonomous: New team leaders are enrolled in a Studytube module automatically from AFAS, with a role-play practice tool.
lenses.ambitious: Every team leader practises a difficult conversation before having it, which today almost none do.
lenses.joy: Fewer rewrites of bad files; more real coaching.
lenses.options: Role-play with several types of employee reaction (angry, silent, in tears) so the manager is ready for each.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP designs the curriculum and the documentation standard and checks quality of files across sites.
reach: Leadership training of the L&D Specialists
Interview training that Recruiters give to hiring managers

tasks.human_edge: Coaching, feedback on how a manager comes across, and judgement whether a file is strong enough for dismissal.
tasks.pattern_why: Training and coaching stay with the HRBP; AI provides practice, drafts and checks.

in_practice.trigger: New team leader in AFAS, start of performance cycle, or a manager opens a performance case.
steps: Studytube enrolment and practice tool for the manager
Manager drafts a performance note with the Word template assistant
Assistant checks it for facts, dates, agreed actions and missing elements
HRBP reviews the note and coaches the manager before the talk
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP approves any formal warning or improvement plan before it is given to the employee.
data_needed: Documentation standard and templates
Case examples (anonymised)
List of new team leaders from AFAS
in_practice.logs_to: Final documents on the employee file in AFAS Profit; training completion in Studytube

evidence.claim: Copilot in Word can draft and review documents against a template.
LLM role-play is used for practising difficult conversations.

risks: Managers use generated text that does not reflect real events
Practice tool trained on real cases leaks personal data
Over-polished files that read as scripted in court
research_questions: How many performance files per year need rework, and how long does that take?
Will team leaders on shifts use a practice tool?
Does the OR need to approve the documentation standard?

tasks.short: Set up ways to measure how employees feel about policies and working conditions, including the complaints procedure.

today.trigger: Yearly employee survey planning, an OR request, or a complaint trend.
steps: Design or adjust the survey with the HR Director and the OR
Run it in Microsoft Forms or a survey tool, with paper for some shift workers
Maintain the complaints procedure and the confidential adviser arrangement
Collect results in Excel
today.time_sinks: Design rounds with stakeholders and getting response from shift workers.

lenses.faster: The copilot drafts the survey in Dutch, Polish and English and checks question wording, cutting design rounds.
lenses.autonomous: Short pulse questions run quarterly by QR code at the site canteens, with results collected without manual entry.
lenses.ambitious: Listening becomes continuous per site and shift rather than one survey a year, so problems show months earlier.
lenses.joy: No more typing up paper forms; more time acting on what people say.
lenses.options: Several survey designs (short pulse, full yearly, topic-specific after a change) to pick from with the OR.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP owns the listening system: what is asked, how often, how results are shared and what is done with them.
reach: Survey work of the People Analytics Analyst
OR consultation preparation for the HR Director

tasks.human_edge: Trust that answers are anonymous, agreement with the OR, and handling complaints confidentially.
tasks.pattern_why: Designing the method is judgement and consultation work; AI helps draft and translate.

in_practice.trigger: Survey cycle planning or a request from the OR.
steps: Copilot drafts the question set and translations
HRBP and OR agree content and anonymity thresholds
Forms runs the pulse by QR code and Teams
Results flow to a Power BI page with a minimum group size
in_practice.human_gate: OR and HR Director approve the survey and the reporting rules.
data_needed: Site and team structure from AFAS
Earlier survey questions and results
Complaint counts by category
in_practice.logs_to: Survey design and approvals on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Employee listening products run pulse surveys and analyse comments.
LLMs translate survey questions well enough for a native speaker to check.

risks: Small groups break anonymity
OR may see monitoring as surveillance (WOR art. 27)
Survey fatigue
research_questions: What response rate do shift workers give on a QR pulse in a pilot site?
What anonymity threshold will the OR accept?
Does the company already hold a licence that covers Viva Glint?

tasks.short: Make reports and presentations on employee satisfaction and related data for management and the OR.

today.trigger: Survey results are in, a quarterly management meeting, or an OR meeting.
steps: Export survey results and absence and turnover data
Build charts in Excel and put them in PowerPoint
Read open comments and write a summary
Present to management and the OR
today.time_sinks: Building charts and summarising comments by hand.

lenses.faster: Power BI produces the standard pages and an LLM groups comments into themes, so the report is a review rather than a build.
lenses.autonomous: When the survey closes, a draft report per site and a summary for management are produced automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every team leader gets their own results with suggested actions, instead of one company slide deck.
lenses.joy: No more chart copying; time goes to the discussion of what to do.
lenses.options: Versions for management, the OR and team leaders from the same data, each with its own focus.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP sets the report standard and checks the story and the themes, not the charts.
reach: Reporting work of the People Analytics Analyst
Absence reporting for the HR Director

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what matters, framing hard messages for management and the OR, and answering questions in the room.
tasks.pattern_why: Charts are deterministic in Power BI; the comment summary is an LLM step a person checks.

in_practice.trigger: Survey closes or a reporting date arrives.
steps: Power BI refreshes the standard satisfaction, absence and turnover pages
LLM groups comments into themes with counts and example quotes (anonymised)
Copilot drafts a short narrative and slides
HRBP checks themes against the raw comments and edits the message
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP approves the report before it goes to management or the OR.
data_needed: Survey results
Absence and turnover from the AFAS extract
Site and team structure
in_practice.logs_to: Final report on SharePoint with the data date

evidence.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint can create slides from a document or data.
Copilot in Power BI can write narrative summaries of report pages.

risks: Quotes that identify an employee
Themes that overstate a minority view
Presenting AI summaries without checking the raw comments
research_questions: How close are LLM themes to an HRBP's own coding on last year's comments?
How many hours did the last report take?
Can the narrative stay within the anonymity rules agreed with the OR?

role.altitude: The HRBP moves from answering questions and building reports to running the HR knowledge base, case precedent, matching rules and listening system that managers and employees use directly, and checking their quality.
reach: Tier-one policy and contract questions from the HR Administrators
Retention and survey analysis from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Internal mobility and interview training from the Recruiters
Manager training content with the L&D Specialists
Allowance and overtime questions for the Payroll Specialist
role.ceiling_note: About a third of the role's time can be freed, mostly from policy questions, preparation and reports; conversations, conflict, trust with the OR and legal judgement stay human, and AVG, works council consent and EU AI Act limits slow anything that ranks or monitors people.
skills_to_grow: Writing and maintaining a policy knowledge base and approved interpretations
Reading data in Power BI and checking AI summaries against the source
Designing small retention experiments and measuring them
Running DPIAs and OR consultations for new HR tools
role.ambitious_version: Three HRBPs act as owners of a self-service HR system for 1,200 employees and 300 flex workers: answers in their own language on any shift, a quarterly retention plan per site tied to 90-day retention, and every team leader prepared for hard conversations, with the HRBPs spending most of their time on the cases and managers that need them.
